::: {#exm-hers-conditional-odds-ratio-reversible}

#### Reversing the roles of treatment and exercise within diabetes strata in HERS

In @exm-hers-odds-ratio-reversible, the roles of hormone therapy and regular exercise are reversed among all the women.
Here the same two [odds ratios](#def-odds-ratio) are computed separately for the women with diabetes and the women without it:

```{r}
#| label: hers-conditional-or-reversed
#| code-fold: false
or_by_diabetes <- sapply(c("no", "yes"), function(z) {
  counts <- table(
    HT = hers$HT[hers$diabetes == z],
    exercise = hers$exercise[hers$diabetes == z]
  )
  ht <- "hormone therapy"
  c(
    ht_odds_ratio = unname(
      (counts[ht, "yes"] / counts["placebo", "yes"]) /
        (counts[ht, "no"] / counts["placebo", "no"])
    ),
    exercise_odds_ratio = unname(
      (counts[ht, "yes"] / counts[ht, "no"]) /
        (counts["placebo", "yes"] / counts["placebo", "no"])
    )
  )
})
or_by_diabetes
```

The first row compares the [odds](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-odds) of hormone therapy between the women who exercise regularly and those who do not.
The second row compares the odds of regular exercise between the hormone therapy and placebo groups.
Among the women without diabetes the two odds ratios are `r round(or_by_diabetes[1, "no"], 3)` and `r round(or_by_diabetes[2, "no"], 3)`, and among the women with diabetes they are `r round(or_by_diabetes[1, "yes"], 3)` and `r round(or_by_diabetes[2, "yes"], 3)`.
In each stratum the two agree, as @thm-conditional-odds-ratio-reversible states.
The stratum odds ratios differ from the [odds ratio](#def-odds-ratio) `r round(or_hat, 3)` of @exm-hers-odds-ratio for all the women, because the theorem equates the two odds ratios within a stratum, not either one with the marginal odds ratio.

:::
